_note: M3 predator tutorial, in the director's order: an automatic arrival hunt that always fails (story), then zoom in on the dingo and learn its needs one at a time, like the wombat. 'Prey must thrive' and 'too many dingoes' are tips that appear when they happen, not steps. All text is draft for the director to rewrite.

steps.title: Something's stirring
steps.body: A newcomer has come to the park.

steps.title: A lone dingo
steps.body: A dingo has come looking for a home. Dingoes are Australia's top predator, and the park needs one to stay in balance. Click it to see what it needs.

steps.title: No den
steps.body: Dingoes raise their pups in dens: rocky outcrops, hollow logs, or old burrows other animals have left. Place a rocky den or a hollow log close to the dingo's territory.

steps.title: Thirsty
steps.body: Its territory has no water. Place water within reach of its den.

steps.title: Alone
steps.body: Dingoes live in family packs. With prey, water and a den, its family will come to join it.

steps.title: A park in balance
steps.body: Predators and prey now share the park. Bring every species to contentment to pass the harmony gate.

tips.title: Prey must thrive
tips.body: The pack is hungry: there isn't enough prey in its territory for all of them. Predators can only thrive where prey does. Keep the kangaroos content and they'll raise more joeys.

tips.title: Too many dingoes
tips.body: There are more dingoes than the prey here can feed. Rangers sometimes relocate a dingo to a park that needs one. Pick Relocate and click a dingo.

finale.title: Predator and prey
finale.body: The dingoes, kangaroos, wombats and possums are all thriving together. Each one keeps the others in balance.
